newsitem.title: USA: Honeywell buying Measurex for $600 million.
newsitem.headline: Honeywell buying Measurex for $600 million.

text.p: Honeywell Inc., a manufacturer of control systems for home and industry, will acquire Measurex Corp. for $600 million in cash, the companies said Monday.
The announcement sent Measurex's stock soaring over 42 percent, gaining $10.25 to close on the New York Stock Exchange at $34.50 in active trading.
The deal is expected to strengthen Honeywell's position as a supplier of systems, services and products for the pulp and paper industry, the companies said in a statement.
Under the terms of the agreement, which was approved by the boards of directors of both companies, Honeywell agreed to buy all of the outstanding shares of Measurex for $35 a share.
Honeywell fell 62.5 cents to $69.375, also on the NYSE.
The companies acknowledged "that a rationalisation of redundant functions will occur" but did not specify how many people might lose their jobs.

Honeywell makes industrial automation and control systems, including process control applications for the pulp industry, and a broad range of instruments. Measurex makes paper machine integrated control systems.
Honeywell employs 53,000 people in 95 countries and had 1996 sales of $7.3 billion. Measurex has offices in 34 countries and had 1996 sales of $287 million.
"It looks like a good deal for both parties," said one industry analyst who asked not to be named.

Jeffrey Sprague at Cowen & Co. said the two companies' operations will fit together well in supplying systems for the paper industry. "This will make Honeywell a one-stop shop" for paper makers, he said.

"We see this transaction as a way to unite the particular strengths of each of our companies," Measurex Chairman David Bossen said. "In this way, we'll be able to deliver a complete suite of automation solutions for pulp and paper manufacturers, extending from the woodyard to the shipping dock."
The merger should provide opportunities for stronger growth for Honeywell in the pulp and paper industry as well as reductions in costs, the companies said.

The business unit will be run within Honeywell Industrial Automation and Control by John Gingerich, who has been president of Measurex. He will report to Markos Tambakeras, president of Honeywell Industrial Control.
